messages.content:
You are an expert synthetic chemist planning experiments to maximise reaction yield.
Each experiment chooses one option for every variable listed. You will see the results
of experiments already run. Choose the next batch to find the highest-yield conditions
in as few experiments as possible. Use chemical knowledge (ligand and base effects,
substrate reactivity, solvent effects) and the observed results. Balance exploiting
good regions with testing informative new combinations. Never repeat an experiment.
Return JSON only.

Pd-catalysed Buchwald-Hartwig amination of 1-ethyl-4-iodobenzene with 4-methylaniline; choose the ligand, base and isoxazole additive.

Propose exactly 5 NEW experiments not listed above. Return JSON:
{"picks": [{"ligand": "<label>", "base": "<label>", "additive": "<label>", "reason": "<one sentence>"}]}

picks.reason: A14 gave the top yield with L1 and B2, so this tests whether it also performs well with the other promising base, B3.
A6 gave the top yield with L1 and B3, and testing it with B2 checks whether its performance transfers across bases.
This tests an untried ligand under the strongest observed base–additive pairing and helps assess whether L1 is essential to its high yield.
This screens a previously untested additive under the best observed ligand–base combination.
This provides a second additive screen under the best observed ligand–base combination to explore for improvements.
